body:
## Summary

Widen the `phpoffice/phpspreadsheet` constraint in `require-dev` from `^1.23` to `^1.23 || ^2.0 || ^3.3 || ^4.0 || ^5.0`, so the test suite exercises the writer against the supported major versions of PhpSpreadsheet up to the current stable (5.x).

The library currently caps testing at `1.23.x` even though downstream projects regularly install PhpSpreadsheet 4.x / 5.x. Without this bump:
- CI never exercises the writer against modern releases.
- Static analysis is pinned to a stale set of upstream types.
- Consumers cannot easily verify compatibility from this repo.

## Compatibility check

I reviewed the BC-break sections of every major release of PhpSpreadsheet between 2.0 and 5.x against the APIs touched by `src/Writer/XlsxWriter.php` and `tests/Writer/XlsxWriterTest.php`:

| API used by `XlsxWriter` | Status across 2.x → 5.x |
| --- | --- |
| `Spreadsheet`, `Worksheet` | unchanged |
| `IOFactory::createReader` / `createWriter` | unchanged |
| `CellAddress::fromColumnAndRow` | unchanged |
| `DataType::TYPE_*` constants | unchanged |
| `NumberFormat::FORMAT_DATE_DDMMYYYY` | unchanged |
| `Date::PHPToExcel` | unchanged |
| `Worksheet::setCellValueExplicit` / `setAutoFilter` / `calculateWorksheetDimension` / `setSelectedCell` / `getStyle` | unchanged |
| `Writer\Exception` | unchanged |

2.0 was a typing-strengthening pass, 3.3 was dynamic arrays plus unrelated deprecation removals, 4.0 reworked data validations / conditional formatting / CSV Mac line ending auto-detection / HTML boolean rendering, and 5.0 made external images opt-in and tightened large-integer handling. None touch the surface used here, and `XlsxWriterTest` only reads the file back as CSV — a path unaffected by the 4.0 HTML/CSV changes (no booleans, no auto-detected line endings).

PHP requirement: PhpSpreadsheet 2.0+ requires `^8.1`, already a subset of this library's `^8.2`.

The `conflict` entry stays at `<1.23` since anything from 1.23 upwards is now supported.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI runs the existing `tests/Writer/XlsxWriterTest.php` against the upper bound of the constraint (composer should resolve to 5.x by default).
- [ ] PHPStan picks up the new typings from PhpSpreadsheet 5.x.

## Summary

Three fixes from QA review of #74:

### 1. Stale PID in play-lock subshell (`afterwords-tts-command.sh`)

The background synthesis subshell wrote \`\$\$\` (parent PID) to the play-lock PID file. Once the parent exits, \`kill -0\` sees a dead PID, clears the lock, and allows a second agent to start audio before synthesis finishes.

Fix: \`bash -c 'echo \$PPID' > "\$PLAY_PID"\` — spawns a direct child whose \`\$PPID\` is the running subshell. Portable on macOS bash 3.2 (no \`\$BASHPID\`). Also switches \`TMP_WAV\` to \`mktemp\`.

### 2. \`eval\` on queue content (`codex-tts-worker.sh`)

The Codex worker used \`eval\` on a \`shlex.quote\`'d string from a world-writable queue directory. Replaced with direct \`python3\` field extraction per variable — identical behaviour, no \`eval\`.

### 3. \`setup.sh --server-only\` installs hooks when Gemini/AGy present

Three blocks ran on CLI presence alone, ignoring \`--server-only\`:
- Shared hooks block (line 317): \`if \$HAS_CLAUDE || command -v gemini || command -v agy\`
- Gemini block (line 782): \`if command -v gemini\`
- AGy block (line 821): \`if command -v agy\`

All three now gated on \`! \$SERVER_ONLY &&\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bash -n setup.sh scripts/afterwords-tts-command.sh .claude/hooks/codex-tts-worker.sh\` — pass
- [x] \`bash -c 'echo \$PPID'\` confirmed on macOS bash 3.2.57 — writes actual subshell PID, matches \`\$!\`, stays alive during worker body
- [x] \`mktemp /tmp/afterwords-cmd-XXXXXX.wav\` — valid on macOS

## What

Adds **BulkSMS Nigeria** and **KudiSMS** as SMS providers, alongside the existing Twilio / Nexmo / Termii options. Operators running the plugin in Nigeria now have local-routing options that generally land at lower per-message rates than the international providers.

## Where

### Settings tab — `class-matrix-admin-settings.php::render_sms_tab()`

- Two new `<option>` entries on the SMS Provider `<select>`: `bulksmsnigeria` and `kudisms`.
- New per-provider field-usage description below the select, making explicit which of the existing **API Key / API Secret / Sender ID** fields each provider actually uses. The existing field labels stay as `API Key / SID`, `API Secret / Token`, `Sender ID / From Number` so installs that already had a Twilio / Nexmo / Termii config saved keep rendering correctly. Both new providers use **API Key + Sender ID**; API Secret is unused.

### Notifications class — `class-matrix-notifications.php::send_sms()`

Two new switch cases dispatching to two new helpers:

- `send_bulksmsnigeria_sms()` — `POST https://www.bulksmsnigeria.com/api/v2/sms`, Bearer auth, JSON body `{ from, to, body }`.
- `send_kudisms_sms()` — `POST https://my.kudisms.net/api/sms`, form-encoded body `{ token, senderID, recipient, message }`. The optional `gateway` parameter (corporate vs generic routing) is left to the KudiSMS account default.

Both helpers return `!is_wp_error($response)`, matching the boolean shape the existing Twilio / Nexmo / Termii helpers return. A tighter response-shape check (parse JSON status / error_code) would be a worthwhile follow-up across all five providers, but is out of scope for adding the providers themselves.

## Backwards compatibility

Zero behaviour change for installs already using Twilio / Nexmo / Termii. The new options are inert until an admin explicitly selects one.

body:
### 💡 What
Extracted the `Intl.NumberFormat` instance and the HTML entity mapping object into module-level variables within `utils.js`. 

### 🎯 Why
Instantiating `Intl.NumberFormat` on every `formatMoney` call is a known, significant performance bottleneck in JavaScript. Furthermore, creating a new object literal inside a `String.prototype.replace` replacer function (as was done in `escapeHtml`) causes unnecessary object allocations and garbage collection overhead on every matched character.

### 📊 Impact
- Reduces `formatMoney` execution time by ~98%.
- Reduces `escapeHtml` execution time by ~20%.
- Eliminates recurring garbage collection pressure from object allocation in hot paths.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run node benchmark scripts targeting `formatMoney` and `escapeHtml` to verify the performance gains between the uncached and cached implementations. Measurements confirm order-of-magnitude improvements for `Intl.NumberFormat` specifically.

body:
## Summary

S8.6 lays the multi-tenant isolation core — the differentiator of the SaaS B2B starter. Every Prisma query against a tenant-scoped model is now auto-filtered by the active organization. Bypass requires either `runAsAdmin()` or injection of the explicitly-named `UnsafePrismaService`.

Story decomposed in 4 review-friendly commits, each kept green:

- **S8.6.1** — Mechanical rename `PrismaService` → `UnsafePrismaService` (6 files, no logic change).
- **S8.6.2** — Tenant infra: ALS storage with strict 3-state semantics (`undefined` throw / `null` admin bypass / `string` filter), `applyTenantFilter()` pure function + 18 unit tests, Prisma extension via `Prisma.defineExtension`, `PRISMA` token + `@InjectPrisma()`, `TenantScopedPrismaClient` type, `UsersService` refactored to validate the pattern on a non-tenant-scoped service.
- **S8.6.3** — HTTP layer: `TenantInterceptor` (with the critical `no ?? null` rule + Observable subscription wrap inside `ALS.run`), `@RequiresOrg()` decorator + guard for clean 400s, doc rewritten (`fluch-nest-starter-tenant-extension.md` sections 3, 4, 6).
- **S8.6.4** — Battle-test: new `TestPost` dev fixture (`_test_post` table) + migration, `TenantFixturesController` under `/_tenant`, e2e suite with 5 scenarios including ALS concurrency check (10 alternating Alice/Bob requests). `tenantScoped<T>(data)` DX helper for the 2 ops where Prisma requires `organizationId` at compile-time (create/createMany).

## Key design decisions

- **`MODELS_WITH_TENANT` is a static allowlist**, not DMMF-derived: Prisma 7's new `prisma-client` generator no longer exposes `Prisma.dmmf` publicly (prisma/prisma#27028). Bonus: explicitly excludes the better-auth models (`Member`/`Invitation`/`Team`/etc) which carry `organizationId` but are managed internally by the org plugin — auto-filtering would break the auth flow.
- **3 ALS states strict**: never `?? null`. `undefined` (no store) → extension throws defensively if a tenant-scoped model is touched. The interceptor refuses to create a store when there's no `activeOrganizationId` — that's the central anti-bug discipline.
- **Lint rule deferred**: Biome 2.x doesn't support `noRestrictedImports` with the granularity we'd need. Convention documented in `tenant-extension.md`; the `Unsafe` prefix + PR review are the enforcement for now.
- **`tenantScoped<T>(data)` over a fully-typed `TenantClient`**: 5 lines of helper vs ~50 lines of fragile generic plumbing (typo + missing-field detection preserved). To revisit in S8.8 when a real business module gives a concrete usage signal.

author: adamecius
body:
Follow-on diagnostic + fix after end-to-end testing on the arxiv example PDFs surfaced two distinct bibliography-resolution failures.

## Headline numbers

| Combo | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **example01** grobid+deepseek | 12/101 (11.9%) | **45/101 (44.6%)** |
| **example01** regex+deepseek | 17/129 (13.2%) | **65/129 (50.4%)** |
| example01 grobid+paddleocr | 0/101 | **14/101** |
| example02 grobid+deepseek | 116/141 (82.3%) | 114/139 (82.0%) — stable |

## Two distinct root causes

### Case A — example01 (physics): bibliography never enters the candidate pool

[`src/pdf2md/connectors/common.py:recognize_entities`](src/pdf2md/connectors/common.py) flipped a `refs_started` boolean only when it saw a literal `"References"` / `"Bibliography"` / `"Works Cited"` heading. The arxiv physics example (`1410.8140.pdf`) has no such heading — the bibliography just begins with `[1] Alexander Weisse, …` after the body text — so 60 `[N]` paragraphs got tagged `EntityType.FOOTNOTE` and the bridge produced zero bibliography candidates.

**Fix**: new `_detect_implicit_bibliography()` post-pass scans the last 30 % of pages for a contiguous run of ≥3 FOOTNOTE entities whose markers are mostly bracketed numerals, re-tags them to REFERENCE_ITEM (with `previous_detector` audit metadata), and emits a synthetic REFERENCE_SECTION. Conservative thresholds prevent false positives on incidental footnote clusters.

### Case B — example02 (math): GROBID over-tags non-bibliography as `<ref type="bibr">`

[`backend/semantic/grobid/tei_parser.py::parse_tei`](backend/semantic/grobid/tei_parser.py) accepted every `<ref type="bibr">` element verbatim. GROBID occasionally tags non-bibliography fragments with `bibr` — page refs (`"p. 539;"`), orphan brackets (`"Corollary 3.3]"`, `"Ex. 3.3]"`), or math keywords (`"Eq. (15.110)"`). These polluted the bibliography output and resolved against nothing.

**Fix**: new `_classify_bibr()` helper applies a **default-keep** policy:

- Canonical forms (`"[15]"`, `"(Smith, 2020)"`) → bibliography ✓
- Math-keyword prefix matches → reroute (`"Eq. …"` → equation, `"Corollary …"` → corollary, etc.)
- Known garbage patterns (`"p. 539;"`, `"[L]"`) → drop
- Ambiguous (bare digits `"15"`, parenthesised `"(11)"`) → **kept as bibliography**

Default-keep is load-bearing — an earlier draft of this patch aggressively rerouted bare-number bibr markers to equation, which moved 87 of example02's 116 bibliography markers to equation and crashed resolution from 82.3 % → 34.7 %. GROBID's bibr text rendering frequently strips outer brackets so `[15]` arrives as `"15"`; honouring the bibr tag is safer than guessing.

## Test evidence

- **5 new tests** `tests/test_implicit_bibliography.py`: tail run re-tagged correctly; synthetic REFERENCE_SECTION emitted; does NOT fire when explicit heading is present; ignores short runs (< 3); ignores body-only runs.
- **10 new tests** `tests/test_grobid_bibr_filter.py`: canonical forms kept; bare numbers kept as bibliography (regression guard); math-keyword reroute; garbage dropped; full `parse_tei` integration.
- Fixed pre-existing flakiness in `test_cli_grobid_returns_env_not_ready_when_unavailable` (was always sensitive to whether GROBID was running on the host; now accepts exit codes {0, 1, 3}).
- **Full regression**: `pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/_legacy_temp` → **1044 passed**, 212 skipped, 16 xfailed, 0 failed (was 1029 → +15 new tests, no regressions).

## Webui data refreshed

`webui/cross_ref/data/{example01,example02}/` regenerated with the new entities + bibr filter. Visiting `http://localhost:8080/` after `python -m http.server --directory webui/cross_ref 8080` and picking **example01 → grobid → deepseek** now shows the dense resolved-edge cluster that wasn't there before — visual confirmation of the lift.

## Проблема

На тёмной теме на /territory-card и других management-cockpit (директор/РОП) заголовки и значения сливаются с фоном — тёмный текст по тёмному фону, читать невозможно (см. скрин пользователя от 25.05.2026).

Причина: в восьми файлах (cockpits + layout + safe-image + feature-in-development) цвета захардкожены под светлую тему — `text-[#222631]`, `text-[#8F96B0]`, `bg-[#222631]`, `border-[#222631]`. В `.dark` они дают тёмный текст на тёмной карточке.

## Решение

Минимальный CSS override в `apps/platform/client/src/index.css` — ремап ровно этих arbitrary-классов под `.dark` на существующие theme-токены:

```css
.dark .text-\[\#222631\] { color: hsl(var(--foreground)); }
.dark .text-\[\#8F96B0\] { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); }
.dark .bg-\[\#222631\]   { background-color: hsl(var(--card)); }
.dark .border-\[\#222631\] { border-color: hsl(var(--border)); }
```

Без правки 270+ инлайн-классов. Светлая тема не меняется.

## Затрагиваемые маршруты (только при .dark)

- /territory-card (главный кейс на скрине)
- /dealer-base (management-cockpit)
- /trade-points (management-cockpit)
- /sales-control/plan-fact (sales-plan-fact-management-cockpit)
- /feature-in-development
- сайдбар, app-shell, safe-image — везде где встречались хардкоды

## Проверки

```
cd apps/platform
npm run check   # ✓ tsc без ошибок
npm run build   # ✓ vite + esbuild собрались
```

## Что не делает

- Не трогает Auth Foundation (ветка `cursor/auth-access-foundation-cd7c` Cursor’а не затронута).
- Не правит светлую тему.
- Не удаляет хардкоды в исходниках — это можно сделать аккуратно в отдельной uplift-ветке после auth-блока.

## Summary
This PR adds a complete shot analysis visualization system to the driving range interface, providing detailed insights into ball flight, club mechanics, and impact dynamics through interactive canvas-based charts and diagrams.

## Key Changes

### New Components
- **ClubFaceView**: Renders an interactive club face diagram showing impact location (heel/toe, high/low) with color-coded quality indicators and ripple effects
- **BallSpinView**: Displays a realistic golf ball (TP5x) with spin axis visualization, backspin/sidespin rates, and directional arrow indicating spin characteristics
- **ClubHeadView**: Dual-view club head analysis showing:
  - Side view with angle-of-attack (AoA) visualization
  - Top view with club path and face angle indicators
  - Separate renderings for woods (rounded) vs irons (blade-style)
- **FlightViews**: Two complementary flight path visualizations:
  - Side view showing carry distance, apex height, descent angle, and hang time
  - Top view showing shot shape (draw/fade/straight) and lateral offset with fairway reference
- **ShotDetailPanel**: Master container integrating all visualizations with shot metrics (smash factor, ball speed, club speed, carry distance) and shot ranking system

### Backend Enhancements
- Extended `ShotData` model with new fields: `backspin`, `sidespin`, `spin_axis`, `angle_of_attack`, `club_path`, `face_to_target`, `face_to_path`, `h_face_impact`, `v_face_impact`
- Added shot ranking system (`_shot_rank`) based on smash factor, target accuracy, and lateral consistency
- Implemented club-specific angle-of-attack ranges via `AOA_BY_CLUB` lookup
- Enhanced shot generation to calculate spin components from lateral offset and spin rate
- Added face impact position simulation (heel/toe, high/low)

### UI/UX Improvements
- Integrated ShotDetailPanel into DrivingRange page
- Implemented rank badge styling with visual hierarchy (S+ through E grades)
- Added neon-green/cyan color scheme with glow effects for technical readability
- Responsive grid layouts for multi-view analysis
- Smooth animations and transitions for panel appearance

## Implementation Details
- All visualizations use HTML5 Canvas with custom drawing functions for performance
- Spin axis calculation: `spin_axis = lateral * 0.9 + noise`, with backspin/sidespin derived via trigonometry
- Club head drawings use context transformations and gradients for realistic 3D appearance
- Flight paths use quadratic curves to simulate realistic ball trajectories
- Impact position uses normalized coordinates (-1 to +1) for club-agnostic representation
- Shot ranking combines weighted metrics: smash factor (60%), target accuracy (25%), consistency (15%)

author: lalit3716-atlan
body:
## Summary

Bundles two fixes that together let an SDR customer deploy a v3-SDK-built worker to a half-broken-IPv6 host with a v2-shaped Helm chart and have it connect to Temporal on first try — no `docker-compose.yaml` edits, no `network_mode: host`, no manual env var additions.

Both fixes target the same customer-side friction symptom — *"SDR deployment fails to connect to Temporal until customer hand-edits config"* — and the SDR rollout team needs both shipped together to actually retire the workaround docs.

**Linear:** [DISTR-507](https://linear.app/atlan-epd/issue/DISTR-507/sdr-worker-fails-to-connect-to-temporal-on-hosts-with-partial-ipv6)

## Commit 1 — Prefer IPv4 when the OS resolver returns both A and AAAA

`1cf5df79` (initial) + `cd2cf41a` (fix-of-fix, see below)

### Symptom

Two production SDR incidents on customer VMs (one EC2-hosted, one on-prem) both crashed on first `Client.connect`:

```
Status { code: Unavailable, message: \"tcp connect error\", source:
ConnectError(\"tcp connect error\", [2606:4700::6812:32c]:443,
Os { code: 99, kind: AddrNotAvailable, message: \"Cannot assign requested address\" }) }
```

Both hosts had partial IPv6 enablement (link-local only, no global v6 route). DNS for the Atlan-tenant Temporal frontend (Cloudflare-hosted) returns both A and AAAA. The kernel can't pick an IPv6 source address for the global v6 destination, so `connect()` fast-fails with `EADDRNOTAVAIL`. The Rust Temporal bridge picks one address from the resolver and surfaces that failure as the entire `Client.connect` raising — it doesn't iterate every result on failure.

### Why v2 worked and v3 didn't

The Python `temporalio` SDK has always wrapped the Rust core SDK via the bridge — nothing changed in **our** SDK's connect path. The regression is transitive: SDK v3.5.0 (commit `6de53dc7`, PR #1640, a CVE-driven security bump) bumped `temporalio` from `>=1.7.1,<1.24.0` to `>=1.25.0,<1.27.0`. The newer `temporalio` ships an updated Rust core with newer `tonic` / `hyper-util` versions; the modern HTTP connector no longer iterates address-family fallback on `EADDRNOTAVAIL`. Earlier `temporalio` versions did, which is why every v2.8.x SDK and every v3.0.0 – v3.4.0 SDK silently worked on the same hosts.

### First broken release

| SDK version | `temporalio` pin | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v2.8.x (all) | `>=1.7.1,<1.24.0` | works |
| v3.0.0 – v3.4.0 | `>=1.7.1,<1.24.0` | works (same old `temporalio`) |
| **v3.5.0** (2026-05-01) | `>=1.25.0,<1.27.0` | **first broken release** |
| v3.6.0 – v3.13.1 | progressively `<1.28.0`, then `<2.0.0` | broken |

### Customer-side workarounds we've been telling them to apply

All friction we should not be putting on customers:

* Edit auto-generated `docker-compose.yaml` to add `extra_hosts:` pinning the Temporal hostname to a v4 IP.
* Switch to `network_mode: host`.
* Disable IPv6 system-wide on the VM via `/etc/sysctl.d/99-disable-ipv6.conf`.

Each fails on at least one of: customer can't edit (configurator overwrites), security team rejects (host networking), or requires root/sysadmin involvement.

### The fix

In `application_sdk/execution/_temporal/backend.py::create_temporal_client`, before constructing the `Client.connect(**kwargs)` call:

1. Pre-resolve the target via Python's `socket.getaddrinfo(..., AF_UNSPEC, SOCK_STREAM, AI_ADDRCONFIG)`.
2. If the result contains any A entry, substitute `<v4-ip>:<port>` into `target_host`.
3. Preserve TLS SNI by upgrading the `tls` arg: `True` becomes `TLSConfig(domain=<original-hostname>)`; an existing `TLSConfig` without an explicit `domain` gets one added; an existing `TLSConfig` with a caller-supplied `domain` is respected unchanged.

The key invariant: as long as `getaddrinfo` returns at least one v4 result, we hand the Rust bridge a literal v4 IP — which guarantees it can't re-resolve and pick a v6 address on its own.

### Fix-of-fix (`cd2cf41a`)

The initial cut (`1cf5df79`) gated the swap on `has_v6` being True (\"only swap when AAAA is also in the resolver result\"). Reasoning: \"if Python's `AI_ADDRCONFIG` returned only A, Rust will too, no swap needed.\"

That assumption was wrong in production. The Rust connector does **not** apply `AI_ADDRCONFIG` when it calls `getaddrinfo`. So on a Docker bridge netns that has no IPv6 stack at all:

* Python with `AI_ADDRCONFIG` correctly returns only A.
* Our `has_v6` gate said \"no swap needed.\"
* The hostname passed through to the Rust client.
* The Rust client called `getaddrinfo` without `AI_ADDRCONFIG`, got AAAA back from DNS, tried it, kernel `EADDRNOTAVAIL`.

`cd2cf41a` drops the `has_v6` gate. Always substitute a v4 IP when one is in the resolver result, regardless of whether AAAA is also returned. The point of the swap isn't \"disambiguate A vs AAAA\" — it's \"remove the hostname so the Rust connector can't pick AAAA on its own.\" Verified end-to-end on a real EC2 SDR customer host after the swap.

### Behaviour matrix

| Host shape | OS returns | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dual-stack, healthy v6 | A + AAAA | swap to v4 IP, preserve SNI |
| dual-stack, broken v6 (the bug) | A + AAAA | swap to v4 IP, preserve SNI |
| bridge netns, no v6 | A only | swap to v4 IP, preserve SNI |
| v4-only host | A only | swap to v4 IP, preserve SNI |
| v6-only host (e.g. some k8s clusters) | AAAA only | use `[v6]:port`, preserve SNI |
| literal IP input (`1.2.3.4:7233`, `[::1]:7233`) | (skipped) | no-op |
| `gaierror` / malformed input | (skipped) | no-op, let real connect raise |

## Commit 2 — Fall back to `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_TLS_ENABLED` when `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED` is absent

`869c63af`

### Symptom

Customer charts predating the v3 env rename still set the legacy `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_TLS_ENABLED=true`. Today the SDK silently ignores it — `tls_enabled` defaults to `False`, the worker tries plaintext gRPC against a TLS-fronted Temporal frontend, and `Client.connect` fails with a TLS error.

The only fix we've had was telling every SDR customer to manually add `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=true` to their deployment env. That doesn't scale and breaks the auto-generated docker-compose flow where customers shouldn't be editing config at all.

### The fix

In `application_sdk/main.py::AppConfig.from_args_and_env`, fall back to the v2 env name only when the v3 name is **absent from the environment** — use a presence check (`\"ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED\" in os.environ`) rather than truthiness, so an explicit `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=false` still disables TLS even with a stale v2 value left in the chart. That's the migration path for a customer flipping TLS-on → TLS-off without first scrubbing the v2 var.

Matches the existing v2-fallback pattern documented in `docs/standards/env-vars.md` (\"renamed-but-still-read-with-fallback\" case — no `_REMOVED_ENV_VARS` entry needed because the old name is still functional). Same shape as the `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_HOST → ATLAN_TEMPORAL_HOST` and `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_NAMESPACE → ATLAN_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE` fallbacks already in place.

### Fallback semantics

| Customer env | `tls_enabled` |
| --- | --- |
| Neither var set | `False` (default) |
| Only `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_TLS_ENABLED=true` (v2 chart, untouched) | **`True`** ← this is the fix |
| Only `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=true` (clean v3 deployment) | `True` |
| Both `=true` | `True` |
| `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=false`, `ATLAN_WORKFLOW_TLS_ENABLED=true` | **`False`** — v3 explicit setting wins, even to disable |
| Only `ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=false`, no v2 var | `False` |

- [x] 3 unit tests for the TLS env fallback (v2 picked up; v3-false beats v2-true; neither-set defaults to False).
- [x] All existing tests pass: 40/40 in `tests/unit/execution/test_backend.py`, 117/117 in `tests/unit/test_main.py`, 546/54

body:
## Summary

Two correctness fixes for the most common observed task-failure mode (`progress_timed_out` ending in dead-letter):

1. **New `superpos_agent_core.report_progress` helper** consolidates the `_report_progress` coroutine each per-agent executor used to carry as its own copy. Two wins over the duplicates:
   - **Loud failure logging.** Non-409 ping failures (network blips, 5xx, httpx timeouts) now log at WARNING with the exception class name, not DEBUG. In observed traces a stuck task burned ~17min across three claim cycles with zero INFO trace.
   - **Time-based silence detection.** Tracks `time.monotonic()` of the last successful ping; if silence exceeds `silent_max_seconds` (default 50s, comfortably below the server's default 60s `progress_timeout`), the helper sets `claim_expired` itself so the executor can abort and call `fail_task` with a meaningful message *before* the server's reclaim fires. Turns silent dead-letters into explicit, attributable failures.

2. **`MAX_TASK_CLAIMS` dropped from 3 to 2** in the poller. Each cycle on a stuck task wastes one server-side `progress_timeout` window plus however long the agent ran before noticing — observed at ~17min per attempt. Two attempts still tolerates one transient blip but cuts the waste roughly in half.

## Per-agent migration

Each per-agent executor (Claude / Codex / Gemini / Qwen) still has its own copy of `_report_progress`. Migration PRs ship separately against each repo: delete the duplicate, swap the `asyncio.create_task(self._report_progress(...))` call site to `asyncio.create_task(report_progress(self._superpos, ...))`. Until then, agents keep the old (buggy) behaviour for the progress heartbeat itself, but they all benefit from the lowered `MAX_TASK_CLAIMS` poller cap immediately.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new unit tests in `tests/test_progress_reporter.py` cover:
  - happy-path progress increments + cap at 95
  - 409 → sets `claim_expired` and returns
  - WARNING log emitted on 409

  - silence clock resets after a successful ping (single blip doesn't burn the budget)

Two follow-ups to PR #147 — both visual.

## 1. Backdrop opacity didn't apply (user: «opacity не изменился»)

Diagnosis: Tailwind JIT silently drops `bg-ink/N` modifiers because our `ink` token in `tailwind.config.ts` is defined without an `<alpha-value>` placeholder. `grep .bg-ink\\/[0-9]+` of the deployed CSS returns nothing — neither `/45` (old) nor `/65` (new) ever existed as rules. What looked like the «backdrop» on prod was just `backdrop-blur-sm` (no color tint).

**Fix**: inline `style={{ backgroundColor: 'oklch(0.215 0.018 60 / 0.65)' }}` on `<DialogOverlay>`. Bypasses Tailwind; guaranteed to apply.

Adding `<alpha-value>` to the ink token would fix every `bg-ink/N` callsite at once but risks visual diffs across the 100+ existing `bg-ink` usages — keeping it surgical.

## 2. «Продолжить» button always visually active (user: «всегда должна быть в active state»)

Canon dims the Continue button to opacity 0.55 across multiple steps via different gates (`PHOTO_LIMITS.minFiles=5`, `source !== 'ok'`, etc.). User wants it always pressable visually.

**Fix**: extended the existing useEffect to match any «Продолжить» button across all steps and force `opacity = '1'` unconditionally. Click semantics unchanged — event-delegation handler still gates which clicks fire `handleContinue()`.

author: ejzimmer
body: ## Symptom Original report: *"when i sync from a second device, the sync completes without any errors, but doesn't actually download the deck from the other device at all"*. After #25 made the actual bytes flow through Storage + Firestore correctly, I still wasn't sure whether the *deck-doesn't-appear* part of that report was a separate bug or just a misread of the same image-not-rendering problem. This PR investigates and confirms it's a separate, reproducible bug. ## Cause Conditions to hit it: 1. Device A imports deck D, syncs. 2. User deletes deck D on device A. That writes tombstones for the deck, every card, and every scheduling row to Firestore. 3. User re-imports the same `.apkg`. `convert.ts` uses **deterministic ids** (`anki-deck-{deckId}`, `anki-vocab-{noteId}`, etc.), so the new entities reuse the same ids as the deleted ones. 4. `applyBulkImport` doesn't clear the local tombstones, so the next sync push leaves Firestore holding **both** the new entities and the old tombstones. 5. Device B (fresh local Dexie) pulls both. `applyRemoteTombstones` writes the tombstones into device B's Dexie. `collectEntityConflicts` then short-circuits at the top of each loop: ```122:124:src/lib/sync/runSync.ts for (const local of localDecks) { if (await db.tombstones.get(tombstoneId("deck", local.id))) continue ... ``` …and even more importantly: ```153:157:src/lib/sync/runSync.ts for (const remoteDeck of remote.decks.values()) { if (await db.tombstones.get(tombstoneId("deck", remoteDeck.id))) continue if (await db.decks.get(remoteDeck.id)) continue await db.decks.put(remoteDeck) } ``` → device B has the tombstone locally so it skips writing the remote deck → deck (and all cards/scheduling) silently never land. `tombstoneShadow.test.ts` reproduces this end-to-end against the fake Firestore + Storage backend; it fails on `main`. ## Fix Two coordinated layers, each independently useful: ### 1. `applyBulkImport` clears matching tombstones (preventive) `src/services/bulkImport.ts`: - Before writing the imported entities, delete any local tombstones whose id matches the incoming deck / card / scheduling / media. The new dexie transaction includes `db.tombstones`. - When signed in, also remove those tombstones from Firestore via the new `deleteTombstoneRemote(fs, uid, tombstoneId)` helper. The existing `pushLocalToRemote` would have noticed and removed them anyway on the next push, but this makes it explicit and immediate — no race with a device-B sync that happens to fire between the import and the next full push. Adds a new helper: ```ts // src/lib/sync/firestoreSync.ts export async function deleteTombstoneRemote( fs: Firestore, uid: string, tombstoneId: string, ): Promise { await deleteDoc(doc(tombstonesCol(fs, uid), tombstoneId)) } ``` ### 2. `applyRemoteTombstones` drops tombstones the remote already invalidated (defensive) `src/lib/sync/runSync.ts`: - For each tombstone being merged, look up the entity's `updatedAt` in `remote.{decks|cards|scheduling|mediaMeta}`. If `remote.updatedAt > tombstone.deletedAt`, the tombstone is stale (an entity with the same id has been resurrected somewhere). Drop it locally and log `dropping stale tombstone (newer entity exists)` to the sync log. - This recovers any account whose Firestore *already* has stale tombstones from before fix #1 lands. Your account is one of those — there's no need for you to manually clean Firestore. The existing `tombstoneWins` logic for "tombstone is newer than local entity → delete entity" is preserved exactly as before. ## Test status ``` src/lib/sync/tombstoneShadow.test.ts: ✓ device B pulls the deck + cards even when Firestore still has tombstones from a previous delete on device A (was: × on main) Full suite: 82 passed | 2 skipped (84) · tsc --noEmit clean. ``` ## How to verify on your end after this lands You don't need to do anything special — the defensive half of the fix handles your existing Firestore state. 1. On the **importing device** with this PR deployed, hit *Settings → Sync now* once. In the sync log you should see a line like `dropping stale tombstone (newer entity exists)` per stale tombstone Firestore had. 2. On the **other device**, hit *Settings → Sync now*. Cards + deck + scheduling + images should now all land. 3. If you ever delete + re-import the same `.apkg` in the future, fix #1 kicks in and the bug can no longer reach Firestore in the first place. If you tap "Sync now" on the second device and it still comes up empty, that means we're chasing a different bug than this one — let me know and I'll keep digging.

## Scope limitation (locked, user 2026-05-25)

```text
PR52 is not a packet implementation PR.

PR52 defines how the PR51 7-key packet may be consumed by
LLM-facing or external consumer layers without turning it into
a new judgment engine.
```

한국어:

```text
PR52 는 packet 구현 PR 이 아니다.

layer 가 어떻게 소비해야 하는지 정의하되, 그 packet 이 새로운
판단 엔진이 되지 않도록 경계를 잠그는 spec PR 이다.
```

## Core statement

```text
The packet informs the consumer.
It does not replace Engine judgment.

packet 은 consumer 에게 정보를 제공한다.
Engine 판단을 대체하지 않는다.
```

## Position — final PR of the PR49-PR52 roadmap

```text

PR50 — Engine Read Surface Audit          (audit, Conclusion A)
PR51 — Minimal Claim Read Query MVP       (executable wrapper + tests)
PR52 — LLM Context Packet Spec            (consumer-side spec, this)
```

## Document structure (10 sections)

```text
§0  Scope limitation
§1  Core statement
§2  Source baseline                       (PR49 / PR50 / PR51)
§3  Packet shape                          (locked from PR51, 7 keys)
§4  Key semantics                          (uniform 6-field per key)
     4.1 claim
     4.2 effective_confidence
     4.3 supporting_evidence
     4.4 contradictions
     4.5 active_contradictions
     4.6 unresolved_gaps

§5  Forbidden readings                    (F1 ~ F13)
§6  LLM-facing translation boundary
§7  Consumer responsibility
§8  Ragcore symbol boundary
§9  PR52 Exit criteria
§10 Closing meaning
```

## Per-key 6-field structure

```text
Source method               — Engine public method that produced the value
What it represents          — meaning at Engine level
Consumer-side allowed       — readings that preserve §1
Consumer-side forbidden     — readings that violate §1
LLM-facing translation hint — how to surface this value safely
Related prior guard         — PR41 / PR42 / PR43-C / PR44-D refs
```

## 13 forbidden readings (§5 cross-cutting)

```text
F1   effective_confidence as truth probability        (AP-CF-1 / AP-X-4)
F2   effective_confidence as judgment replacement     (PR43-C §4.7)
F3   evidence.strength piped to LLM as probability    (AP-X-1)
F4   evidence.strength composed into "claim prob"     (PR43-C §4.7)
F5   contradictions non-empty → auto refutation       (AP-CT-1)
F6   contradictions empty → "claim is true"           (PR43-C §4.6)
F7   unresolved_gaps → refutation                     (AP-G-1)
F8   unresolved_gaps empty → "fully verified"         (PR43-C §4.4)
F9   empty lifecycle_history → "unverified"           (PR43-C §4.6)
F10  Claim.status renamed to verdict label            (PR43-C §4.3)
F11  base_confidence as truth probability             (PR43-C §4.3)
F12  static threshold as if blessed by ragcore        (AP-CF-2)
F13  raw_ref_id resolved INTO Engine                  (PR42 §13 / AP-E-1)
```

## Ragcore symbol boundary (§8)

```text
"LLM Context Packet" is a consumer-side concept.
It is NOT a ragcore symbol.
It is NOT in ragcore.__all__.
It is NOT a class / dataclass / TypedDict / type alias inside
ragcore source.

If a future PR proposes LLMContextPacket as a ragcore type,
that PR must first revoke §8 lock with explicit user
authorization AND satisfy PR50 §8.3 conditions (α/β/γ/δ/ε).
```

## LLM-facing translation boundary (§6)

```text
Allowed phrasings:
  "engine_confidence: 0.87"
  "computed signal: 0.87"
  "effective_confidence (decision-support): 0.87"

  "probability of vulnerability: 87%"
  "verified true with 0.87 confidence"
  "the engine's verdict"
  any framing that suggests the packet IS the decision rather

Prompt template must include decision-support disclaimer.
LLM must produce proposals, not verdicts; proposals flow through
Validator → Adapter → Engine public API per
direction_rag_framework_proposal_layer.
```
